title: Deformable DETR: Deformable Transformers for End-to-End Object Detection
layout_note: Three columns: a legend box (top-left) above the input image and its pyramid of image feature maps (bottom-left); a tall dashed 'Encoder' container (centre) in which three stacks of feature maps rise bottom to top with a dashed '× 4' box around the middle stack; a dashed 'Decoder' container (right) with columns of query bars rising from 'Object Queries' at the bottom to the box-prediction image at the top.
grouping: Encoder and decoder are large dashed black rectangles with bold labels in their bottom-right corners; repeated layers are wrapped in a thinner grey dashed rectangle marked '× 4'. A light-grey legend box explains the three dashed-arrow colours (purple: encoder deformable self-attention, red: decoder deformable cross-attention, black: decoder self-attention). A red curly brace groups the top multi-scale stack and a red dashed line runs from it to every decoder layer.
shapes_depth: Every feature map is the input photo itself, faded and drawn as an oblique parallelogram, stacked three deep for the three scales. Sampling locations are drawn on the maps as small purple triangles (encoder) or red squares, with a purple dot for the reference point; dashed purple arrows run from sampled points on lower maps to the reference point above. Object queries are columns of three narrow vertical bars (red, green, peach) per layer, with black dashed arrows between bars for self-attention. The output is the faded photo as a parallelogram with coloured box outlines.
proposed_highlight: The proposed attention is not boxed; it is drawn as its mechanism: sparse sampling points marked as glyphs on the feature-map images and dashed arrows from them to a reference point, with the arrow colour (purple vs red) keyed in the legend to encoder vs decoder use.
lesson: Draw sparse attention by putting the sampling points as small coloured glyphs directly on faded, tilted copies of the input photo at each scale, with dashed arrows from them to the query's reference point.
notes: Venue and year from the PDF's first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2021'). The faded photo planes are many embedded images in the crop (refs crop recorded 32), excluded from the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: deformable attention drawn on the feature maps themselves: dashed purple arrows run from a handful of sampled points (triangles) on stacked multi-scale feature maps to one query point (dot), so sparse sampling across scales is the visual signature

relations.form: photo-textured feature-map stacks at three scales, with purple triangles marking sampled keys and a purple dot the query they feed; decoder cross-attention samples drawn as red squares on the top stack
left to right: image and its feature pyramid, the encoder frame (stacks bottom to top), then the decoder frame (bottom to top) topped by the bounding-box photo
a grey dashed box marked x4 around the middle encoder stack and around the middle decoder layers marks the repeated layers
a red brace gathers the encoder's top feature maps and red dashed arrows branch into each decoder layer's red query bar

channels.colour: attention type, keyed top left: purple = encoder multi-scale deformable self-attention, red = decoder deformable cross-attention, black = decoder plain self-attention; the decoder bars' red/green/orange identify individual object queries, a second meaning
channels.shape: triangle = sampled key location, dot = query location, red square = cross-attention sample; tilted photo slab = a feature map; vertical bar = an object query
channels.line: dashed arrows = attention (colour-coded type); solid black arrows = data flow up the decoder
channels.frame: large black dashed frames = Encoder and Decoder; grey dashed frame = repeated block (x4)

quality.strengths: The mechanism is drawn on its structure (sampled points on multi-scale maps) and the attention kinds are separated by a keyed colour; encoder and decoder are framed units in reading order with repeated layers boxed x4.
quality.weaknesses: Dozens of crossing purple dashed lines over faded photos make the encoder busy; colour is used for both attention type and per-query identity (red bar vs red cross-attention arrow collide); the red cross-attention arrows run a long way down the gutter between frames; the input image-to-encoder arrows cross diagonally.

insights.structure: Three columns: image and its multi-scale feature pyramid at bottom-left, a tall dashed Encoder frame in the middle with three stacks of skewed feature maps (middle stack boxed 'x 4'), and a dashed Decoder frame on the right with rows of red/green/orange query bars topped by the box-prediction photo.
insights.data: Feature maps are drawn as tilted, faded copies of the real football photo stacked in threes, with purple triangles as sampled points and purple/red dots as reference points; object queries are small coloured vertical bars.
insights.emphasis: Three dashed-arrow colours, explained in a top-left legend, separate deformable self-attention (purple), deformable cross-attention (red) and plain decoder self-attention (black), so the sparse sampling is the visual signature.
insights.flow: Purple dashed lines run from sampled points on the pyramid up into a reference dot in the encoder; the encoder output is braced and sent right by red dashed lines into every decoder layer, which reads bottom to top to the predictions.
insights.avoid: Dozens of crossing purple dashed lines over the faded photos make the encoder busy; fewer samples would show the mechanism just as well.

arrangement.units: An unframed input pyramid, then a dashed Encoder frame and a dashed Decoder frame, each with an inner grey dashed 'x 4' repeat box.
arrangement.inputs_as: a real photo with a pyramid of image feature maps; object queries at the bottom of the decoder
arrangement.losses_at: none drawn; the output is a photo with coloured bounding boxes above the decoder
arrangement.shared: repeated layers collapsed into a grey dashed box marked x 4 in both encoder and decoder
